key_insight: SCAPS-1D optimization shows that an In2S3/Cu2NiGeS4/MoTe2 stack can substantially boost thin-film solar-cell performance by improving carrier separation, reducing recombination, and tuning layer/device parameters.
engineering_relevance: The study provides practical design rules for high-efficiency, earth-abundant chalcogenide photovoltaics, highlighting how interface engineering and defect control can push CNGS devices toward experimentally relevant performance.
method: Simulated a CNGS thin-film solar-cell architecture with In2S3 as the electron-transport layer and MoTe2 as the hole-transport layer.
Analyzed band alignment, electric field, carrier profiles, and generation-recombination behavior to identify loss mechanisms.
Optimized thickness, doping, defect density, recombination, resistance, temperature, and illumination conditions in SCAPS-1D.
evidence_signal: The optimized device is reported to reach 28.44% PCE with 0.984 V VOC, 34.39 mA/cm2 JSC, and 84.04% FF under AM1.5G illumination at 300 K, improving on the previously reported 6.25–21.17% range for CNGS cells in the study.
watch_item: The results are computational predictions, so real-device performance may be lower if interface quality, material stability, or fabrication-induced defects differ from the assumed model.
paper_title: Device Engineering and Performance Optimization of Cu2NiGeS4 Thin-Film Solar Cells with In2S3/MoTe2 Charge-Selective Layers: A Computational Study
